definitions.explanation: An adnominal meaning 'unknown' or 'unfamiliar,' placed directly before a noun. Most often describes a person one has never met.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}かれた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: A stranger asked me for directions.

examples.japanese: {見知|みし}らぬ⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧になった。
examples.english: I felt uneasy in an unfamiliar place.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜道|よみち}→夜道：17541_yomichi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{見知|みし}らぬ⟦{男|おとこ}→男：00561_otoko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かけられて、⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まった→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧。
examples.english: A strange man called out to me on the dark road, and I instinctively froze.

notes:
A {連体詞|れんたいし} (pre-noun adjectival): it appears only directly before a noun and does not conjugate. Literally 'not having seen and come to know.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見知|みし}らぬ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a stranger; an unknown person
- {見知|みし}らぬ⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧: an unfamiliar place
- {見知|みし}らぬ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧: an unfamiliar face

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: someone one doesn't know — more everyday and conversational
- {見知|みし}らぬ is slightly more literary, common in narration and writing
